doc: SCHEMA.md's filter micro-syntax, applied end to end: a query in, the ids it leaves out. Browser-renderer only -- table-view.el's `/' is a plain substring over the row, with no grammar to hold to this. The `state:*...*' cases are a renderer's half of a producer meta: which keywords are in a group is the producer's to say, so the only term decidable here is the empty cell SCHEMA puts in `*active*'. Most cases share the file's `view'; a case may carry one of its own, either whole or as {"$ref": NAME} naming one of `views'.

cases.name: a column key makes a predicate
= is an alias for :
a badge value matches whole and case-insensitively
a badge value does not match by substring
a leading hyphen negates
a single-valued field ORs its repeats
cases.doc: AND would always be empty, so repeating `state' means either.

cases.name: a multi-valued field ANDs its repeats
cases.doc: `tag' declares `multi', so a row must carry both.

cases.name: & separates a token like whitespace
distinct keys AND
none matches the empty cell
the active meta matches the empty cell
cases.doc: SCHEMA puts an unstated row in `*active*' -- live work. The keyword half of the group needs the producer's sets, so locally the empty cell is the whole answer.

cases.name: the inactive meta has no empty-cell half
cases.doc: An entry nobody marked done is not done, so the two metas do not partition the column.

cases.name: negating the active meta drops the empty cell
state:none is that same empty cell, asked for by name
cases.doc: Unchanged by the meta, and now a subset of it.

cases.name: a key with nothing typed narrows nothing
a date-shaped column matches by prefix
and not in the middle
a text column matches by substring
org tag text is free text, never a predicate
an unknown key is free text too
a quoted token is free text with spaces
free text reads the whole row
a bare hyphen negates the empty term, which matches everything
an empty query filters nothing
planned is the date columns taken together
cases.doc: A row is planned when EITHER date cell holds anything; `due' has only a deadline.

cases.name: planned:none is a row nobody put a day on
a planned value is the date prefix, over every date column at once
so a prefix one column misses can still be met by the other
cases.doc: Only the deadline falls in that decade of the month.

cases.name: and a prefix is a prefix, never a substring
planned repeats OR, being single-valued like the columns it reads
planned with nothing typed narrows nothing
negating planned drops what it matched
planned ANDs with a column predicate like any distinct key
cases.doc: The agenda's shape, spelled with a concrete keyword: which keywords are `*active*' is the producer's to say, so a vector states the half decidable here.

cases.name: planned shadows a tag spelled like it
cases.doc: `:planned:' is in the vocabulary and `planned' still reads as the date key, the way a column key would shadow it.
